questions.question: List the steps of the accounting cycle for a business with credit sales, naming the journal and the subsidiary ledger used for credit sales.
questions.expected_answer: (1) Transaction occurs; source document created (duplicate invoice for credit sales). (2) Recorded in subsidiary journals: CRJ, CPJ, debtors journal (DJ), later CJ. (3) Posted to the general ledger and to the debtors ledger (one account per debtor). (4) Trial balance and debtors list prepared. (5) Financial statements prepared and nominal accounts closed (Grade 10). The cycle repeats each period.

questions.question: Analyse the effect on the accounting equation of a credit sale of R3 600 at a mark-up of 50 percent on cost.
questions.expected_answer: Cost = 3 600 × 100 ÷ 150 = R2 400. Sales part: A +3 600 (debtors control increased); OE +3 600 (income: sales). Cost part: A -2 400 (trading stock decreased); OE -2 400 (expense: cost of sales). Net: A +1 200; OE +1 200; L 0.

questions.question: Analyse a debtor's payment of R6 000 and explain why it does not affect owner's equity.
questions.expected_answer: A +6 000 (bank increased) and A -6 000 (debtors control decreased); OE 0; L 0. The income was already recorded when the goods were sold; the payment only exchanges one asset (debtor) for another (bank), so recording it as income would count the sale twice.
